rows.grounds: bahuvrīhi-style compound epithet of the goddess; kakāra denotes the syllable ka
compound epithet indicating devotion or intentness toward the sound kaka

items.question: What form and sonic devotion further characterize the goddess associated with the syllable ka?
premises: The goddess is described as having the form of the syllable ka.
The goddess is described as devoted to the sound kaka.
These attributes continue the series of ka-related epithets.
items.inference: The goddess is further defined by embodiment of the ka-syllable and devotion to the kaka sound.
uncertainties: The precise nuance of parāyaṇā as devotion, intentness, or absorption is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: She has the form of the syllable ka and is devoted to the sound 'kaka'.
